name: Bemba
notes: Bemba (Chibemba, Guthrie M.42), Bantu language of the Northern, Luapula and Copperbelt provinces of Zambia. Five vowel qualities a/e/i/o/u with a phonemic length distinction, not marked in the standard orthography. Prenasalized voiceless and voiced series (mp/mb, nt/nd, ntʃ/ndʒ, nk/ŋɡ, plus prenasalized fricatives mf, ns, nsh) are single (complex) segments; Bemba has a strict CV syllable structure. ⟨ng'⟩ /ŋ/ is the bare velar nasal, contrasting with prenasalized ⟨ng⟩ /ᵑɡ/, the same convention as Nyanja and Yao. /b/ is realized as the approximant/fricative [β] in most positions, including word-initially, alternating with [b] when derived from nasal-triggered hardening (n+β → mb); it is not a simple intervocalic-only allophone. Bemba is a tone language with two level tones (H/L, mora as tone-bearing unit) with extensive lexical and grammatical (melodic) tone, downstep and tonal spreading; tone is not marked in the standard orthography (Hamann & Kula 2015).
